config.title: useImperativeHandle

intro.title: useImperativeHandle
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a form with a custom input component that allows a parent component to programmatically focus the input field. You will learn how to use the React hook `useImperativeHandle` to customize the instance value that is exposed when using `ref` on a child component. The main technologies involved are React functional components, TypeScript for type safety, and the `forwardRef` API to pass refs through components. This will help you understand how to control child component behavior from a parent in a type-safe way.
intro.usecase: useImperativeHandle is commonly used in component libraries and complex UI systems where parent components need to directly control child component behavior. For example, in form libraries, a parent form component might use useImperativeHandle to call a child input's focus() or validate() methods when the user clicks a "Clear All" or "Validate All" button. In dashboard applications with multiple interactive panels, a dashboard container might expose reset() or refresh() methods on child chart or widget components. This pattern is also useful in custom video players where the parent player needs to control play(), pause(), and seek() methods on child video components from external controls.

objectives: Implement a parent component that creates a ref and passes it to a child component
Configure a child component to expose custom methods using useImperativeHandle
Initialize a forwardRef wrapper to enable ref forwarding between components
Manipulate child component state and behavior through exposed imperative methods
Apply TypeScript interfaces to define the shape of exposed imperative handles
Control when imperative handle methods are recreated using dependency arrays
Integrate useImperativeHandle with other React hooks like useState and useEffect

steps.title: Import React, useRef, useImperativeHandle, and forwardRef
steps.instruction: Import React, useRef, useImperativeHandle, and forwardRef from 'react'.
steps.hint: Use a single import statement with curly braces to import multiple named exports from 'react'.
steps.analogousExample:
// Importing multiple hooks from React
import React, { useState, useEffect } from 'react';
steps.seedCode: // Import React, useRef, useImperativeHandle, and forwardRef from 'react'
steps.expectedOutcome: The necessary React hooks and utilities are imported for the useImperativeHandle lesson.
successCriteria: React, useRef, useImperativeHandle, and forwardRef are imported from 'react'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.

steps.title: Create a parent component with TypeScript interface
steps.instruction: Create a functional parent component called ParentComponent with an empty return statement.
steps.hint: Define a component using either function ParentComponent() {} or const ParentComponent = () => {}. Make sure it returns null or an empty JSX fragment for now.
steps.seedCode:
import React, { useRef, useImperativeHandle, forwardRef } from 'react';

// Create your ParentComponent here
steps.expectedOutcome: A ParentComponent function is defined with an empty return statement.
successCriteria: The code contains a functional component named ParentComponent that returns null or an empty fragment.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you've created a component named ParentComponent and it has a return statement (even if it returns null).
steps.feedbackWrong: The component wasn't created correctly. Please create a functional component called ParentComponent with an empty return statement.

steps.title: Create a child component with forwardRef
steps.instruction: Create a child component named ChildComponent using forwardRef. It should accept props and a ref parameter, and return a simple div element.
steps.hint: Use forwardRef from React to create a component that can receive a ref from its parent. The component should have two parameters: props and ref.
steps.expectedOutcome: A ChildComponent function is created using forwardRef, accepting props and ref as parameters and returning a div element.
successCriteria: ChildComponent is defined using forwardRef, has props and ref parameters, and returns a JSX element (like a div).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you're using forwardRef correctly and that your component accepts both props and ref as parameters.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component wasn't created correctly. Remember to use forwardRef and define a function that takes props and ref, then returns JSX.

steps.title: Define TypeScript interface for child component methods
steps.instruction: Define a TypeScript interface named ChildMethods that declares two methods: focusInput (returns void) and clearInput (returns void).
steps.hint: Create an interface using the 'interface' keyword, specifying the method signatures.
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have a TypeScript interface that defines the methods the child component will expose via useImperativeHandle.
successCriteria: The ChildMethods interface is defined with focusInput and clearInput methods, both returning void.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure both methods (focusInput and clearInput) are declared and return void.
steps.feedbackWrong: The interface definition is missing or incorrect. Define an interface named ChildMethods with the required methods.

steps.title: Add useImperativeHandle to child component
steps.instruction: Inside your ChildComponent, implement the useImperativeHandle hook to expose methods defined in the ChildMethods interface.
steps.hint: Call useImperativeHandle inside the component body, passing the ref and a function that returns an object with the methods you want to expose.
steps.expectedOutcome: The ChildComponent will have useImperativeHandle implemented, ready to expose specific methods to the parent.
successCriteria: useImperativeHandle is called inside ChildComponent with the ref parameter and a function returning an object.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure useImperativeHandle is called with the ref and a function that returns an object.
steps.feedbackWrong: The useImperativeHandle hook is not properly implemented. Check the syntax and parameters.

steps.title: Create input element in child component
steps.instruction: Inside your ChildComponent, add an input element with a ref attached to it.
steps.hint: Use the standard <input> tag and assign a ref attribute to connect it to the DOM.
steps.expectedOutcome: The ChildComponent will have an input element that can be controlled via the exposed methods.
successCriteria: An <input> element with a ref attribute is present inside the ChildComponent.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the input element has a ref attribute attached.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you've added an <input> element inside the ChildComponent with a ref attribute.

steps.title: Create ref in parent component
steps.instruction: Inside your ParentComponent, use the useRef hook to create a ref with the type ChildMethods | null. Initialize it with null.
steps.hint: Call useRef<ChildMethods | null>(null) to create the ref. Store it in a variable (e.g., childRef).
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: creating a typed ref
const inputRef = useRef<HTMLInputElement | null>(null);
steps.expectedOutcome: The parent component will have a ref that can hold a reference to the child component's methods.
successCriteria: ParentComponent contains a useRef call with type ChildMethods | null, initialized to null.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using useRef with the correct type (ChildMethods | null) and initializing it with null.
steps.feedbackWrong: The ref wasn't created correctly. Use useRef<ChildMethods | null>(null) inside ParentComponent.

steps.title: Render child component with ref in parent
steps.instruction: Inside the return statement of your ParentComponent, render the ChildComponent and pass the ref you created as a prop.
steps.hint: Remember to pass the ref as a prop to the ChildComponent. The prop name should match what the ChildComponent expects (typically 'ref').
steps.expectedOutcome: The ParentComponent will render the ChildComponent with the ref attached, enabling the parent to call methods on the child.
successCriteria: ChildComponent is rendered inside ParentComponent's return statement with the ref prop correctly passed.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're rendering ChildComponent and passing childRef as a prop (typically named 'ref').
steps.feedbackWrong: The ChildComponent isn't rendered with the ref prop. Check that you're using the correct ref variable and prop name.

steps.title: Add buttons in parent to call child methods
steps.instruction: Inside the ParentComponent's return statement, add two buttons with onClick handlers that call the child methods via the ref.
steps.hint: Use the childRef.current property to access the exposed methods (focusInput and clearInput).
steps.expectedOutcome: The parent component will have two buttons that can trigger the child's focus and clear methods.
successCriteria: Two buttons are added with onClick handlers that call childRef.current?.focusInput() and childRef.current?.clearInput().
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added buttons, but make sure both onClick handlers correctly call the child methods via the ref.
steps.feedbackWrong: The buttons or their onClick handlers are missing or incorrect. Check the hint and try again.

steps.title: Add TypeScript safety checks for ref methods
steps.instruction: In the ParentComponent, add conditional checks (if (childRef.current)) before calling the focusInput and clearInput methods on the ref to ensure type safety.
steps.hint: Before calling childRef.current.focusInput() or childRef.current.clearInput(), check if childRef.current exists to avoid runtime errors.
steps.expectedOutcome: The buttons will safely call the child component's methods only when the ref is available, preventing potential runtime errors.
successCriteria: Both button click handlers include conditional checks (if (childRef.current)) before calling the ref methods.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some checks, but make sure both button handlers include the conditional check before calling the methods.
steps.feedbackWrong: The conditional checks are missing. Remember to check if childRef.current exists before calling focusInput() or clearInput().
